dragon.prompt: Make a six-frame flight cycle of the EXACT supplied approved flame dragon head. This is production source art for Cuồng Long Loạn Vũ in a 2D wuxia RPG. Exactly 3 columns and 2 rows with equally sized square cells, 1536×1024 landscape, chronology in reading order. Pure black #000000, substantial margins in every cell; no label, frame outline, props or text. One complete head in each cell, identical size, facing strictly right, and the same tip of the nose at the same coordinates in each cell, around x=470,y=280 relative to its own square. Keep the identity: East Asian dragon formed out of orange fire qi, two forked horns swept backwards, round raised nose with a visible nostril, short dark angular eye, an S-shaped flame whisker, and two separate subtly pointed jaws, dark open gap between. No bird beak, no body, wings, neck or physical skin. Keep the widest part in the THREE broad swept-back flame tongues shown in the reference, upper, center and lower, spreading slightly apart. Match the exact phoenix-like palette and flame rhythm of the reference: dark maroon and deep red edges, strong orange flame mass, selective amber ridges, a tiny pale slit at the eye, no bloom. Deliberate clean pixel clusters readable at native 80 px width; no glows, speckle, thin detail, or excessive texture. Start in the provided pose. Then flex the three trailing flame tongues in a subtle traveling wave and let one or two small sparks peel off behind; the muzzle and horns stay locked, jaw may flex by one native pixel. Six distinct, coherent sequential phases, sixth naturally leads into first. The trailing mane stays flared throughout, as in the approved artwork. Preserve original silhouette proportions and visual character at all times.
